prompt:
Research the official rate limits of the public GitHub REST API for unauthenticated and authenticated requests. Cite the GitHub documentation page and quote the numbers.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The GitHub REST API enforces different rate limits depending on whether the request is authenticated or unauthenticated. Below are the official limits as documented by GitHub.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "For requests using Basic Authentication, OAuth, or personal access tokens (classic), you can make up to 5,000 requests per hour." | CLAIM: Authenticated requests via Basic Auth, OAuth, or classic personal access tokens are limited to 5,000 requests per hour.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "For unauthenticated requests, the rate limit allows for up to 60 requests per hour." | CLAIM: Unauthenticated requests are limited to 60 requests per hour.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "For requests made with a fine-grained personal access token, you can make up to 15,000 requests per hour." | CLAIM: Authenticated requests using a fine-grained personal access token are limited to 15,000 requests per hour.
